rules.validated: needs independent evidence: a black-box workflow (tests/blackbox.mjs) or a registered release gate that exercises it end to end
rules.production-ready: needs validated plus operational evidence (durable storage, monitoring, alerting in production); nothing has it yet

capabilities.label: Local persistence (IndexedDB, incremental writes)
Backup and restore
Progress photos: encrypted on the device, copied encrypted to the vault, carried by encrypted backups
capabilities.note: each image an attachment with a content hash; retraction, orphans, duplicates, failed uploads, partial restore and quota are handled and tested; the cloud copy needs the sync server

capabilities.label: Erase everything
Food logging with portions
Two records of one food that disagree, settled by a declared rule
capabilities.note: the nutrients that differ are named with both values; each record is checked against its own macros (4/4/9, the food sheet’s own check); the first of your own entry, USDA laboratory analysis, the USDA branded label and Open Food Facts that agrees with itself is used, and the other is kept visible. Scanning a barcode you already have an entry for offers the record the rule chooses, and the food sheet says why. The order and thresholds are a heuristic contract, not validated

capabilities.label: Training sessions and sets
Corrections and deletions with history
Phase targets reaching Today
Recovery readings changing today's training advice
Readiness and recovery scores backtested against the session that follows
capabilities.note: each past session is scored against each lift’s own last three exposures; the recovery summary, the latent recovery state and the readiness average are rebuilt as the record stood the evening before, beside no information, sleep alone and fatigue alone, and each is scored out of sample (leave one out). A score adds value only if it beats the best simple reading by 5% with a positive correlation. On the demo record all three predict the sessions but no better than fatigue alone, and both recovery screens and the assistant say so

capabilities.label: One plan authority (every plan change through changePlan, one version each)
What was known on a past date
Encrypted sync between devices
capabilities.note: needs a persistent disk; production mode refuses to start without one and without off-host backups

capabilities.label: Verified off-host server backups, restore and health
capabilities.note: tested against a mock S3 that checks signatures and payload hashes; not yet against a real provider

capabilities.label: Adaptive plan
Personal response model
capabilities.note: Hierarchical (Stage E): the phase contexts of a response are pooled toward the person’s own estimate through the shared Bayes engine once two contexts have their own data, and the strength trends of trained regions are pooled the same way before one is called lagging. Partial pooling as in Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis (3rd ed., ch. 5).
capabilities.source: population priors: 3,500 kcal per lb; 0.5 kcal per step per kg (Hall 2008 on the limits of the 3,500 rule); updated by the person’s Responses

capabilities.label: Forecasts that compete for accuracy
Unified optimiser
capabilities.note: a deeper calorie cut is credited with the everyday movement it is expected to cost: the personal NEAT response (steps a day per 10% deficit, Bayesian from a population prior), applied only to the share of the calorie effect still resting on the population figure; each option simulated forward 8 weeks (simulatePolicies): the forecast competition’s winning model for the path with no change, plus each change’s effect counted only if carried out, with an 80% interval; the plan records the simulated outcome when an option is chosen
capabilities.source: Martin et al. 2007 (CALERIE: spontaneous activity falls under energy restriction)

capabilities.label: Marginal returns: the next unit of each dose
capabilities.note: population curves; the sets curve becomes personal (fitted across regions, Bayesian) once the person’s data carry a fifth of it
capabilities.source: Schoenfeld 2017; Pelland 2024; Morton 2018; Paluch 2022; WHO 2020; Wilson 2012; Watson 2015; Garthe 2011; Helms 2014

capabilities.label: Goal conflicts and arbitration on seven dimensions
capabilities.note: declared rules with heuristic contracts; each conflict reports its trade-off, the chosen objective or none, and the expected consequence; the person chooses which goal leads

capabilities.label: Structured explanations: claims, rules and evidence at three levels
capabilities.note: each decision's reasons are claims built from the models' values, rendered simple, analytical or scientific; a published finding supports a rule, never validates it; every decision answers the eight questions of W-045 with a trace to its observations; each confidence says whether it is a rating or calibrated

capabilities.label: Body composition: fat and lean trajectories
capabilities.note: the fat-mass rate from the weight trend's partition prior and each body-fat method's own trend (weighted by that method's error, methods never mixed), lean as the remainder; masses only when a measured reading from the last 60 days anchors them
capabilities.source: method errors in BODYFAT_METHOD_SE; the US Navy circumference equation (Hodgdon & Beckett 1984); the partition prior of tissueEnergyDensity

capabilities.label: What a circumference change can mean, site by site
capabilities.note: each site’s change over its recent readings is set against the tape’s error (the person’s own repeats within two days, or a 1 cm working assumption) and counts only beyond 2√2 errors; a change that counts is read with the weight and strength trends for what it is consistent with, and says what the tape cannot separate. A tape measures girth, not tissue. The threshold and working error are a heuristic contract, not validated

capabilities.label: Aerobic fitness: VO2max level and trend
capabilities.note: per modality family, from steady sessions with heart rate and pace or power (a Kalman filter for the level, its intervals scored against the next session); the trend a weighted regression with a prior centred on no change; capacity sits beside the cardio minutes in the capability vector; its 80% interval calibrated by its own one-step-ahead record (self-calibration)
capabilities.source: ACSM metabolic equations; Milanović et al. 2015 (VO2max gains from training)

capabilities.label: Mobility, conditioning, power and speed: field tests and their responses
capabilities.note: five field tests in the quick log (sit-and-reach, knee-to-wall, one-minute heart-rate recovery, countermovement jump, 20 m sprint), each related to its dose (mobility minutes, cardio minutes, lower-body sets) averaged over the four weeks before the test: a population prior per unit of dose updated by the person's own slope through bayesUpdate, with the personal weight; in the capability vector and the physiology card
capabilities.source: stretching and sit-and-reach (Thomas et al. 2018); knee-to-wall reliability (Bennell et al. 1998); heart-rate recovery and training (Daanen et al. 2012) and as a fitness marker (Cole et al. 1999); jump height and plyometric training (Markovic 2007); strength and sprint time (Seitz et al. 2014)

capabilities.label: Why a lift stalled: likely causes named from the record
capabilities.note: a lift the plan reads as flat or falling against its own noise names its likely causes in a stated order: an unapplied progression (the same top set three times running), sets far from failure, readiness below the person’s normal, loss faster than the band in a cut, volume up 30% or more; each with its evidence, threshold, what to do and what would settle it, on “What to change next week”. The thresholds are a heuristic contract, not validated

capabilities.label: Mobility recommendation: limitation, measurement, intervention, expected change, retest, response and uncertainty
capabilities.note: from the knee-to-wall and sit-and-reach tests (quick log or assessment): a left-right difference over two test errors, a gap between active and passive range, a range short of the working reference (a heuristic contract, not validated) or range lost from the person’s own best; the test’s error from the person’s own repeats or the published figure; static or end-range work at 30 more minutes a week; the change expected from the mobility response (population prior updated by the person’s own slope, with its weight); a retest after four weeks on the same protocol; what the earlier reading already shows against the response; and whether one retest can separate the change from the test’s error
capabilities.source: stretching dose and range of motion (Thomas et al. 2018); knee-to-wall reliability (Bennell et al. 1998)

capabilities.label: Cardio as five separate quantities: dose, capacity, expenditure, recovery cost and strength interference
capabilities.note: a cardio change is evaluated on each over a period before and after it: minutes a week, the fitness model’s VO2max estimate (never moved by minutes), kcal above rest from each session’s own MET, relative load (refused when sessions carry no intensity), and strength lift by lift (reported, not attributed). Shown on the cardio experiment before and after it starts
capabilities.source: MET values: the 2024 Adult Compendium of Physical Activities; ACSM metabolic equations for walking, running and cycling

capabilities.label: Causal estimates of each change: interrupted series and matched periods
capabilities.note: each Response's before/after estimate is reported beside an interrupted series (level and rate against the old trend projected to the change, standard errors widened for day-to-day carry-over) and a matched-periods estimate (the same comparison at dates in the person's own record with no change: same weekday and phase, a similar starting trend, Student's t for few periods); a person's deliberate changes, pooled per unit, are an identification strategy of their own. Observational: it rules out drift and regression to the mean, not a cause that arrived with the change; and the day-by-day path without the change (responseCounterfactual): the trend before continued, with what matched periods did on their own where they exist, an 80% band, shown with a chart in each Response’s sheet
capabilities.source: segmented regression of interrupted time series (Wagner et al. 2002, J Clin Pharm Ther); the AR(1) variance factor for a trend regressor; caliper matching (Austin 2011, Pharm Stat)

capabilities.label: Personal knowledge: versions, conflicts and decay
capabilities.note: each Response carries its version and the method version that derived it, and is derived again (a new version naming the one it replaced) when it matures or the method changes; negative knowledge carries its method version and its place among findings about the same change; findings that disagree (two responses beyond their noise, or 'did not work' beside a clear response) are shown side by side with their age weights; in the personal response model each response counts for half as much every 270 days

capabilities.label: Experiment portfolio: the next test by expected information gain
capabilities.note: every lever's ready-made test on one scale: the expected information gain 1/2 ln(1 + s0^2/se^2), with s0 the lever's SD now (widened by half of any disagreement between its findings) and se the outcome's noise over a Response's windows over the dose likely carried out (the person's own response errors where measured over most of both windows); ranked per week of testing; a test that would narrow the estimate by less than 10% is not worth running
capabilities.source: expected information gain for a normal model (Lindley 1956, Ann Math Stat); Bayesian experimental design (Chaloner & Verdinelli 1995, Stat Sci)

capabilities.label: Sensor fusion: one value from several sources
capabilities.note: a measured quantity from two or more sources (told apart by provider or device) is fused on every day: each source put on the reference source’s scale (your preferred one, else the one with the most readings) by its mean same-day difference, each reading weighted by its quality over its source’s measured noise squared, a reading the others contradict set aside when there are three; from readings known by the date asked about only; body fat left to its own reconciliation
capabilities.source: inverse-variance weighting of measurements (e.g. Hartung, Knapp & Sinha 2008, Statistical Meta-Analysis); measurementModel's per-source bias and noise

capabilities.label: User-approved automation: approval policy and audit
capabilities.note: every automated action has a level: view (changes nothing) runs; routine (an undoable record) runs under the standing approval recorded when its rule is turned on; important (the plan, targets, programme, profile, any deletion) never runs on a trigger, only holds a proposal that applies when approved, through changePlan; an undeclared action is important; every decision is in the audit log

capabilities.label: Self-calibration of every interval
capabilities.note: the forecast competition’s calibration made the one rule for every model that makes interval predictions (weight and strength forecasts, aerobic capacity, personal response predictions): the factor that would have made the 80% interval hold 80% of the time, learned on older predictions and checked on newer ones, widening or narrowing the live interval once ten predictions are scored; one report says whether each model’s intervals are honest; and execution probabilities: a backtest (fitted on the older half of the days, scored on the newer half, Brier score against the base rate) and a prospective record (each day’s planned items stamped before the day, scored after it)

capabilities.label: State model (the 'digital twin')
capabilities.note: a mathematical state model, not a validated twin

capabilities.label: Import from Apple Health, Fitbit, Withings and Oura exports and CSV
Live connections to Fitbit, Withings and Oura
capabilities.note: tested against simulated providers only, never a real account

capabilities.label: Garmin, WHOOP, Strava, Polar, Samsung Health, Health Connect, HealthKit
LLM providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, local OpenAI-compatible) through the server
capabilities.note: tested against mock providers that check each protocol; not yet against a real provider. Apple Foundation Models need a native app

capabilities.label: AI proposals: describe a log entry or a meal, suggest a session, explain the plan
capabilities.note: off until consent; read-only tools; validated output; nothing is written until the person confirms

capabilities.label: OCR of labels and photos
Body shape from photos

axes.engineering: the single ladder: not implemented → specified → implemented → integrated → surfaced → validated → production-ready

axisRules.scientific: backtested: scored against the person’s own data by a release gate
axisRules.scientific: prospectively validated: not possible yet: no prospective validation exists
axisRules.personalization: personal: fitted to the person’s own data
axisRules.evidence: independent: needs a black-box workflow or a gate that checks results independently of the implementation
